task: Continue implementing the rate-limiter: ChatGPT planned it, this pack hands the reviewed plan to Claude Code to build, and Codex will review the result.
project_summary: An API needs a per-API-key rate limiter (100 requests/minute, sliding window). One tool planned the approach, a human reviewed it, and the reviewed plan is now being handed to the next tool to implement — then to a third for review.
current_direction: The plan is approved. Claude Code implements against these constraints; Codex then reviews the diff against the same definition of done.

decisions.title: Sliding-window counter in Redis, keyed by API key
decisions.body: Use a Redis sorted set per key with request timestamps; count entries in the trailing 60s window.
decisions.rationale: Chosen during planning as the balance of accuracy and cost; a human approved it before this handoff.
decisions.tradeoffs: Slightly more memory than a fixed-window counter, but avoids the burst-at-the-boundary problem.
decisions.outcome: Approved in review — this is the plan Claude Code should implement, not reopen.

sources.label: MDN — HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
sources.bound_claim: A rate-limited response should use 429 and a Retry-After header

prompts.text: Implement the approved sliding-window rate limiter exactly as specified in the decisions and constraints. Do not redesign the approach. Return the diff plus the tests you added.

constraints: Implement the approved sliding-window design — do not switch to a different algorithm.
Return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when the limit is exceeded.
The limiter must fail open (allow the request) if Redis is unreachable, and log that it did.
boundaries: Handoff record — what each tool did, reviewed, and passes on:
Planning tool produced: the sliding-window design + the 100/min figure.
Human reviewed and approved: the algorithm and the fail-open rule.
This pack carries forward: the approved decision, constraints, and definition of done.
The next tool (implementation) receives: this pack only — not the raw planning chat.
The next tool must return: the diff + tests, for the review tool to check.
what_to_avoid: Re-litigating the algorithm choice that was already reviewed and approved.
Silently failing closed (blocking all traffic) when Redis is down.
open_questions: Should the limit be configurable per key tier, or a single global 100/min for v1?
next_steps: Implementation tool: build the limiter + middleware and add tests for under-limit, at-limit, over-limit, and Redis-down.
Review tool: check the diff against the decision, constraints, and definition of done; flag any deviation.
Human: approve the reviewed result before it merges.
definition_of_done: The middleware enforces 100 req/min per key with a sliding window, returns 429 + Retry-After over the limit, fails open with a log when Redis is down, and has tests for all four cases — matching the approved plan without redesigning it.

recommended_assistant.reason: The plan is approved and reviewed; the next step is a bounded implementation for a coding tool, then a review pass.
